27.s: yady akāryaśataṃ sāgraṃ kṛtaṃ vedaś ca dhāryate | sarvaṃ tat tasya vedāgnir dahaty agnir ivendhanam |
27.d: यद्य् अकार्यशतं साग्रं कृतं वेदश् च धार्यते । सर्वं तत् तस्य वेदाग्निर् दहत्य् अग्निर् इवेन्धनम् ।
27.e: If a hundred improper acts, and even more, have been committed, and the (knowledge of the) [paragraph continues] Veda is retained, the fire of the Veda destroys all (the guilt) of that man just as a (common) fire consumes fuel.

27.s: yathā jātabalo vahnir dahaty ārdrān api drumān | tathā dahati vedāgniḥ karmajaṃ doṣam ātmanaḥ |
27.d: यथा जातबलो वह्निर् दहत्य् आर्द्रान् अपि द्रुमान् । तथा दहति वेदाग्निः कर्मजं दोषम् आत्मनः ।
27.e: As a fire that burns strongly consumes even green trees, even so the fire of the Veda destroys one's guilt caused by (evil) deeds.

27.s: hatvāpi sa imān lokān bhuñjāno 'pi yatas tataḥ | ṛcvedaṃ dhārayan vipro nainaḥ prāpnoti kimcana |
27.d: हत्वापि स इमान् लोकान् भुञ्जानो ऽपि यतस् ततः । ऋच्वेदं धारयन् विप्रो नैनः प्राप्नोति किम्चन ।
27.e: A Brāhmaṇa who remembers the Rig-veda is not tainted by any guilt, though he has destroyed these (three) worlds and has eaten the food of all, (even of the most sinful) men.

27.s: na vedabalam āśritya pāpakarmaratir bhavet | ajñānāc ca pramādāc ca dahyate karma netarat |
27.d: न वेदबलम् आश्रित्य पापकर्मरतिर् भवेत् । अज्ञानाच् च प्रमादाच् च दह्यते कर्म नेतरत् ।
27.e: If (a Brāhmaṇa) relies on the power of the Veda, he cannot find pleasure in sinful acts. Guilt (incurred) through ignorance and negligence is destroyed, not (that of) other (intentional offences).

27.s: tapas tapyati yo 'raṇye munir mūlaphalāśanaḥ | ṛcam ekāṃ ca yo 'dhīte tac ca tāni ca tat samam |
27.d: तपस् तप्यति यो ऽरण्ये मुनिर् मूलफलाशनः । ऋचम् एकां च यो ऽधीते तच् च तानि च तत् समम् ।
27.e: If a hermit subsisting on roots and fruit practises austerities in a forest, and (a householder) recites a single Ri k , the merit of the acts of the one and of the other is equal.

27.s: itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃhayet | bibhety alpaśrutād vedo mām ayaṃ prahariṣyati |
27.d: इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां वेदं समुपबृंहयेत् । बिभेत्य् अल्पश्रुताद् वेदो माम् अयं प्रहरिष्यति ।
27.e: Let him strengthen the Veda by (studying) the Itihāsas and Purāṇas. For the Veda fears a man of little learning, (thinking) 'He will destroy me.'

27.s: vedābhyāso 'nvahaṃ śaktyā mahāyajñakriyākramaḥ | nāśayaty āśu pāpāni mahāpātakajāny api |
27.d: वेदाभ्यासो ऽन्वहं शक्त्या महायज्ञक्रियाक्रमः । नाशयत्य् आशु पापानि महापातकजान्य् अपि ।
27.e: The daily recitation of the Veda and the performance, according to one's ability, of the series of Mahāya g ñ as quickly destroy guilt, even that of mortal sins.

27.s: vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ | tad hi kurvan yathāśaktyā prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim |
27.d: वेदोदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्याद् अतन्द्रितः । तद् हि कुर्वन् यथाशक्त्या प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ।
27.e: Let him daily perform, without tiring, his particular rites which the Veda enjoins. For if he does that according to his ability, he will reach the most blessed state.

27.s: yājanādhyāpanād yaunāt tathaivāsatpratigrahāt | vipreṣu na bhaved doṣo jvalanārkasamo hi saḥ |
27.d: याजनाध्यापनाद् यौनात् तथैवासत्प्रतिग्रहात् । विप्रेषु न भवेद् दोषो ज्वलनार्कसमो हि सः ।
27.e: Through sacrificing for wicked people, through teaching them, through intermarrying with them, and through receiving gifts from them, (learned) [paragraph continues] Brāhmaṇas do not contract guilt, for (a learned Brāhmaṇa) resembles a fire and the sun.

27.s: śaṅkāsthāne samutpanne abhojyabhojyasaṃjñake | āhāraśuddhiṃ vakṣyāmi tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu |
27.d: शङ्कास्थाने समुत्पन्ने अभोज्यभोज्यसंज्ञके । आहारशुद्धिं वक्ष्यामि तन् मे निगदतः शृणु ।
27.e: I will now declare the purification prescribed for (eating) food, regarding which doubts have arisen, whether it may be called fit to be eaten or not. Listen to my words!

27.s: akṣāralavaṇāṃ rūkṣāṃ pibedbrāhmīṃ suvarcalām | trirātraṃ śaṅkhapuṣpīṃ ca brāhmaṇaḥ payasā saha |
27.d: अक्षारलवणां रूक्षां पिबेद्ब्राह्मीं सुवर्चलाम् । त्रिरात्रं शङ्खपुष्पीं च ब्राह्मणः पयसा सह ।
27.e: Let a Brāhmaṇa drink during three days the astringent decoction of the Brahmasuvar k alā plant, unmixed with salt or pungent condiments, and (a decoction of) the Śaṅkhapushpī plant, together with milk.

27.s: palāśabilbapatrāṇi kuśān padmān udumbarān | kvāthayitvā pibed āpas trirātreṇaiva śudhyati |
27.d: पलाशबिल्बपत्राणि कुशान् पद्मान् उदुम्बरान् । क्वाथयित्वा पिबेद् आपस् त्रिरात्रेणैव शुध्यति ।
27.e: Let him drink water, after boiling in it Palāśa and Bilva leaves, Kuśa grass, and (leaves of) lotuses and Udumbara trees; after three days and no more he becomes pure.

27.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam | ekarātropavāsaś ca śvapākam api śodhayet |
27.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् । एकरात्रोपवासश् च श्वपाकम् अपि शोधयेत् ।
27.e: (Subsisting) during one day on each (of the following substances), cow's urine, cowdung, milk, sour milk, butter, and water in which Kuśa grass has been boiled, and fasting on the seventh day purify even (him who fears that he has partaken of the food of) a Śvapāka.

27.s: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ caiva kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā | pañcarātraṃ tadāhāraḥ pañcagavyena śudhyati |
27.d: गोमूत्रं गोमयं चैव क्षीरं दधि घृतं तथा । पञ्चरात्रं तदाहारः पञ्चगव्येन शुध्यति ।
27.e: He who lives during five days on cow's urine, cowdung, milk, sour milk, and clarified butter, is purified by means of (that) Pa ñ k agavya, (the five products of the cow.)

27.s: yavān vidhinopayuñjānaḥ pratyakṣeṇaiva śudhyati | viśuddhabhāve śuddhāḥ syur aśuddhe tu sarāgiṇaḥ |
27.d: यवान् विधिनोपयुञ्जानः प्रत्यक्षेणैव शुध्यति । विशुद्धभावे शुद्धाः स्युर् अशुद्धे तु सरागिणः ।
27.e: He who, in accordance with the rule, uses barley (for his food), becomes pure even by ocular proof. (For) if he is pure, those (barley grains) will be white, if he is impure they will be discoloured.

27.s: haviṣyān prātar āśāṃs trīn sāyam āśāṃs tathaiva ca | ayācitaṃ tathaiva syād upavāsatrayaṃ bhavet |
27.d: हविष्यान् प्रातर् आशांस् त्रीन् सायम् आशांस् तथैव च । अयाचितं तथैव स्याद् उपवासत्रयं भवेत् ।
27.e: (If he makes) three morning meals of food fit for a sacrifice and three evening meals in like manner, and if food given without asking (is his subsistence) in the same manner, (he will thus perform) three fasts.

27.s: atha cet tvarate kartuṃ divasaṃ mārutāśanaḥ | rātrau jalāśaye vyuṣṭaḥ prājāpatyena tat samam |
27.d: अथ चेत् त्वरते कर्तुं दिवसं मारुताशनः । रात्रौ जलाशये व्युष्टः प्राजापत्येन तत् समम् ।
27.e: Now if he is in haste to make (himself pure), (let him) subsist on air during a day, and pass the night standing in water; (that penance) is equal to a Prā g āpatya (K ri k kh ra).

27.s: sāvitryaṣṭasahasraṃ tu japaṃ kṛtvotthite ravau | mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvair yadi na brahmahā bhavet |
27.d: सावित्र्यष्टसहस्रं तु जपं कृत्वोत्थिते रवौ । मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैर् यदि न ब्रह्महा भवेत् ।
27.e: But if at sunrise he mutters the Gāyatrī eight thousand times, he will be freed from all mortal sins, provided he be not the slayer of a Brāhmaṇa.

27.s: yo vai stenaḥ surāpo vā bhrūṇahā gurutalpagaḥ | dharmaśāstram adhītyaiva mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ |
27.d: यो वै स्तेनः सुरापो वा भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः । धर्मशास्त्रम् अधीत्यैव मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ।
27.e: He, forsooth, who has stolen (the gold of a Brāhmaṇa), has drunk spirituous liquor, has slain a learned Brāhmaṇa, or has violated his Guru's bed, will become free from all (these) mortal sins if he studies the Institutes of the sacred law.

27.s: duritānāṃ duriṣṭānāṃ pāpānāṃ mahatāṃ tathā | kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam |
27.d: दुरितानां दुरिष्टानां पापानां महतां तथा । कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं चैव सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ।
27.e: For unlawful acts, for unlawful sacrifices, and for great sins (let him perform) a K ri k kh ra and a K āndrāyaṇa, which destroy all guilt.

27.s: ekaikaṃ vardhayet piṇḍaṃ śukle kṛṣṇe ca hrāsayet | amāvāsyāṃ na bhuñjīta evaṃ cāndrāyaṇo vidhiḥ | evaṃ cāndrāyāṇo vidhir iti |
27.d: एकैकं वर्धयेत् पिण्डं शुक्ले कृष्णे च ह्रासयेत् । अमावास्यां न भुञ्जीत एवं चान्द्रायणो विधिः । एवं चान्द्रायाणो विधिर् इति ।
27.e: Let him add daily one mouthful (to his food) during the bright (half of the month), let him diminish it (daily by one mouthful) during the dark (half), and let him fast on the new-moon day; that is the rule for the K āndrāyaṇa (or lunar penance).

28.s: na strī duṣyati jāreṇa na vipro vedakarmaṇā | nāpo mūtrapurīṣeṇa nāgnir dahanakarmaṇā |
28.d: न स्त्री दुष्यति जारेण न विप्रो वेदकर्मणा । नापो मूत्रपुरीषेण नाग्निर् दहनकर्मणा ।
28.e: A woman is not defiled by a lover, nor a Brāhmaṇa by Vedic rites, nor water by urine and ordure, nor fire by consuming (impure substances).

28.s: svayaṃ vipratipannā vā yadi vā vipravāsitā | balāt kāropabhuktā vā corahastagatāpi vā |
28.d: स्वयं विप्रतिपन्ना वा यदि वा विप्रवासिता । बलात् कारोपभुक्ता वा चोरहस्तगतापि वा ।

28.s: na tyājyā dūṣitā nārī nāsyās tyāgo vidhīyate | puṣpakālam upāsīta ṛtukālena śudhyati |
28.d: न त्याज्या दूषिता नारी नास्यास् त्यागो विधीयते । पुष्पकालम् उपासीत ऋतुकालेन शुध्यति ।

28.s: striyaḥ pavitram atulaṃ naitā duṣyanti karhicit | māsi māsi rajo hy āsāṃ duṣkṛtāny apakarṣati |
28.d: स्त्रियः पवित्रम् अतुलं नैता दुष्यन्ति कर्हिचित् । मासि मासि रजो ह्य् आसां दुष्कृतान्य् अपकर्षति ।
28.e: Women (possess) an unequalled means of purification; they never become (entirely) foul. For month by month their temporary uncleanness removes their sins.

28.s: pūrvaṃ striyaḥ surair bhuktāḥ somagandharvavahnibhiḥ | gacchanti mānuṣān paścānaitā duṣyanti dharmataḥ |
28.d: पूर्वं स्त्रियः सुरैर् भुक्ताः सोमगन्धर्ववह्निभिः । गच्छन्ति मानुषान् पश्चानैता दुष्यन्ति धर्मतः ।
28.e: Women belong first to three gods, Soma (the moon), the Gandharva, and Fire, and come afterwards into the possession of men; according to the law they cannot be contaminated.

28.s: tāsāṃ somo 'dadac chaucaṃ gandharvaḥ śikṣitāṃ giram | agniś ca sarvamedhyatvaṃ tasmān niskalmaṣāḥ striyaḥ |
28.d: तासां सोमो ऽददच् छौचं गन्धर्वः शिक्षितां गिरम् । अग्निश् च सर्वमेध्यत्वं तस्मान् निस्कल्मषाः स्त्रियः ।
28.e: Soma gave them cleanliness, the Gandharva their melodious voice, and Fire purity of all (limbs); therefore women are free from stains.

28.s: trīṇi striyaḥ pātakāni loke dharmavido viduḥ | bhartṛvadho bhrūṇahatyā svasya garbhasya pātanam |
28.d: त्रीणि स्त्रियः पातकानि लोके धर्मविदो विदुः । भर्तृवधो भ्रूणहत्या स्वस्य गर्भस्य पातनम् ।
28.e: Those versed in the sacred law state that there are three acts (only) which make women outcasts, (viz.) the murder of the husband, slaying a learned Brāhmaṇa, and the destruction of the fruit of their womb.

28.s: vatsaḥ prasravaṇe medhyaḥ śakuniḥ phalapātane | striyaś ca ratisaṃsarge śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ |
28.d: वत्सः प्रस्रवणे मेध्यः शकुनिः फलपातने । स्त्रियश् च रतिसंसर्गे श्वा मृगग्रहणे शुचिः ।
28.e: A calf is pure when the milk flows, a bird when it causes fruit to fall, women during dalliance, and a dog when he catches a deer.

28.s: ajāśvā mukhato medhyās gāvo medhyās tu sarvataḥ |
28.d: अजाश्वा मुखतो मेध्यास् गावो मेध्यास् तु सर्वतः ।
28.e: Pure is the mouth of a goat and of a horse, pure is the back of a cow, pure are the feet of a Brāhmaṇa, but women are pure in all (limbs)

28.s: sarvavedapavitrāṇi vakṣyāmy aham ataḥ paraṃ | yeṣāṃ japaiś ca homaiś ca pūyante nātra saṃśayaḥ |
28.d: सर्ववेदपवित्राणि वक्ष्याम्य् अहम् अतः परं । येषां जपैश् च होमैश् च पूयन्ते नात्र संशयः ।
28.e: I will now declare the purificatory texts (which are found) in each Veda; by muttering them or reciting them at a burnt-oblation (men) are doubtlessly cleansed (from sin).

28.s: aghamarṣaṇaṃ devakṛtaṃ śuddhavatyas taratsamāḥ | kūṣmāṇḍāni pāvamānyo durgāsāvitrir eva ca |
28.d: अघमर्षणं देवकृतं शुद्धवत्यस् तरत्समाः । कूष्माण्डानि पावमान्यो दुर्गासावित्रिर् एव च ।
28.e: (They are) the Aghamarshaṇa, the Devak ri ta, the Śuddhavatīs, the Taratsamas, the K ūshmāṇd as, the Pāvamānīs, and the Durgāsāvitri;

28.s: atīṣaṅgāḥ padastobhāḥ sāmāni vyāhṛtīs tathā | bhāruṇḍāni sāmāni ca gāyatraṃ raivataṃ tathā |
28.d: अतीषङ्गाः पदस्तोभाः सामानि व्याहृतीस् तथा । भारुण्डानि सामानि च गायत्रं रैवतं तथा ।
28.e: The Atīshaṅgas, the Padastobhas, and the Sāmans (called) Vyāh ri ti, the Bhāruṇd a Sāmans, the Gāyatra (Sāman), and the Raivata;

28.s: puruṣavrataṃ ca bhāsaṃ ca tathā devavratāni ca | abliṅgaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ tu vācsūktaṃ madhvṛcas tathā |
28.d: पुरुषव्रतं च भासं च तथा देवव्रतानि च । अब्लिङ्गं बार्हस्पत्यं तु वाच्सूक्तं मध्वृचस् तथा ।
28.e: The Purushavrata and the Bhāsa, and likewise the Devavrata (Sāmans), the Abliṅga, the Bārhaspatya, the hymn addressed to Vā k , likewise the Ri k as (called) Madhu;

28.s: śatarudriyam atharvaśiras trisuparṇaṃ mahāvratam | gosūktaṃ cāśvasūktaṃ ca śuddhāśuddhīye sāmanī |
28.d: शतरुद्रियम् अथर्वशिरस् त्रिसुपर्णं महाव्रतम् । गोसूक्तं चाश्वसूक्तं च शुद्धाशुद्धीये सामनी ।
28.e: The Śatarudriya, the Atharvaśiras, the Trisuparṇa, the Mahāvrata, the Gosūkta, and the Aśvasūkta, and the two Sāmans (called) Suddhāśuddhīya.

28.s: trīṇ ājyadohāni rathantaraṃ ca agner vrataṃ vāmadevyaṃ bṛhac ca | etāni japtāni punanti jantūnjātismaratvaṃ labhate yadīcchet |
28.d: त्रीण् आज्यदोहानि रथन्तरं च अग्नेर् व्रतं वामदेव्यं बृहच् च । एतानि जप्तानि पुनन्ति जन्तून्जातिस्मरत्वं लभते यदीच्छेत् ।
28.e: The three (Sāmans called) Ā g yadohas, the Rathantara, the Agnervrata, the Vāmadevya, and the B ri hat, being muttered, purify (all) living beings. (He who sings them) may obtain the recollection of former existences, if he desires it.

28.s: agner apatyaṃ prathamaṃ suvarṇaṃ bhūr vaiṣṇavī sūryasutāś ca gāvaḥ | tāsām anantaṃ phalam aśnuvīta yaḥ kāṃścanaṃ gāṃ ca mahīṃ ca dadyāt |
28.d: अग्नेर् अपत्यं प्रथमं सुवर्णं भूर् वैष्णवी सूर्यसुताश् च गावः । तासाम् अनन्तं फलम् अश्नुवीत यः कांश्चनं गां च महीं च दद्यात् ।
28.e: Gold is the firstborn of Fire, through Vishṇu exists the earth, and the cows are children of the [paragraph continues] Sun; he who bestows as gifts gold, a cow, and land will obtain rewards without end for them.

28.s: uparundhanti dātāraṃ gaur aśvaḥ kanakaṃ kṣitiḥ | aśrotriyasya viprasya hastaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirākṛteḥ |
28.d: उपरुन्धन्ति दातारं गौर् अश्वः कनकं क्षितिः । अश्रोत्रियस्य विप्रस्य हस्तं दृष्ट्वा निराकृतेः ।
28.e: A cow, a horse, gold, (and) land, bestowed on an unlearned Brāhmaṇa who neglects his sacred duties, prevent the giver (from attaining heaven).

28.s: vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā | tilān kṣaudreṇa saṃyuktān kṛṣṇān vā yadi vetarān |
28.d: वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु ब्राह्मणान् सप्त पञ्च वा । तिलान् क्षौद्रेण संयुक्तान् कृष्णान् वा यदि वेतरान् ।

28.s: prīyatāṃ dharmarājeti yad vā manasi vartate | yāvaj jīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇād eva naśyati |
28.d: प्रीयतां धर्मराजेति यद् वा मनसि वर्तते । यावज् जीवकृतं पापं तत्क्षणाद् एव नश्यति ।

28.s: suvarṇanābhaṃ kṛtvā tu sakhuraṃ kṛṣṇamārgajam | tilaiḥ pracchādya yo dadyāt tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu |
28.d: सुवर्णनाभं कृत्वा तु सखुरं कृष्णमार्गजम् । तिलैः प्रच्छाद्य यो दद्यात् तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ।
28.e: But hear (now) the reward of the merit acquired by that man who gives the skin of a black antelope, to which the hoofs are (still) attached and the navel of which is adorned with gold, covering it with sesamum grains.

28.s: sasuvarṇaguhā tena saśailavanakānanā | caturvaktrā bhaved dattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ |
28.d: ससुवर्णगुहा तेन सशैलवनकानना । चतुर्वक्त्रा भवेद् दत्ता पृथिवी नात्र संशयः ।
28.e: 'Without doubt he has bestowed (through that gift) the four-faced earth, together with its caves filled with gold, and together with its mountains, groves, and forests.'

28.s: kṛṣṇājine tilān kṛtvā hiraṇyaṃ madhusarpiṣī | dadāti yas tu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtām iti | sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam iti |
28.d: कृष्णाजिने तिलान् कृत्वा हिरण्यं मधुसर्पिषी । ददाति यस् तु विप्राय सर्वं तरति दुष्कृताम् इति । सर्वं तरति दुष्कृतम् इति ।
28.e: He who, placing on the skin of a black antelope, sesamum, gold, honey, and butter, gives it to a Brāhmaṇa, overcomes all sin.'

29.e: Through liberality (man) obtains all his desires,
(Even) longevity, (and he is born again as) a student of the Veda, possessed of beauty.
He who abstains from injuring (sentient beings) obtains heaven.
By entering a fire the world of Brahman (is gained).
By (a vow of) silence (he obtains) happiness.
By staying (constantly) in water he becomes a lord of elephants.
He who expends his hoard (in gifts) becomes free from disease.
A giver of water (becomes) rich by (the fulfilment of) all his desires.
A giver of food (will have) beautiful eyes and a good memory.
He who gives a promise to protect (somebody) from all dangers (becomes) wise.
(To bestow gifts) for the use of cows (is equal to) bathing at all sacred places.
By giving a couch and a seat (the giver becomes) master of a harem.
By giving an umbrella (the giver) obtains a house.
He who gives a house obtains a town.
He who gives a pair of shoes obtains a vehicle.

29.s: athāpy udāharanti | yat kimcit kurute pāpaṃ puruṣo vṛttikarṣitaḥ | api gocarmamātreṇa bhūmidānena śudhyati |
29.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । यत् किम्चित् कुरुते पापं पुरुषो वृत्तिकर्षितः । अपि गोचर्ममात्रेण भूमिदानेन शुध्यति ।
29.e: Now they quote also (the following verses): Whatever sin a man distressed for livelihood commits, (from that) he is purified by giving land, (be it) even "a bull's hide."'

29.s: viprāyācamanārthaṃ tu dadyāt pūrṇakamaṇḍalum | pretya tṛptiṃ parāṃ prāpya somapo jāyate punaḥ |
29.d: विप्रायाचमनार्थं तु दद्यात् पूर्णकमण्डलुम् । प्रेत्य तृप्तिं परां प्राप्य सोमपो जायते पुनः ।
29.e: 'He who gives to a Brāhmaṇa a vessel filled with water for sipping, will obtain after death complete freedom from thirst and be born again as a drinker of Soma.'

29.s: anaḍuhāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ dattānāṃ dhūryavāhinām | supātre vidhivaddānaṃ kanyādānena tat samam |
29.d: अनडुहां सहस्राणां दत्तानां धूर्यवाहिनाम् । सुपात्रे विधिवद्दानं कन्यादानेन तत् समम् ।
29.e: 'If a gift of one thousand oxen fit to draw a carriage (has been bestowed) according to the rule on a perfectly worthy man, that is equal to giving a maiden.'

29.s: trīṇy āhur atidānāni gāvaḥ pṛthvī sarasvatī | atidānaṃ hi dānānāṃ vidyādānaṃ tato 'dhikam |
29.d: त्रीण्य् आहुर् अतिदानानि गावः पृथ्वी सरस्वती । अतिदानं हि दानानां विद्यादानं ततो ऽधिकम् ।
29.e: 'They declare that cows, land, and learning are the three most excellent gifts. For to give learning is (to bestow) the greatest of all gifts, and it surpasses those (other gifts).'

29.s: ātyantikaphalapradaṃ mokṣasaṃsāramocanam | yo 'nasūyur imaṃ vidvān ācāram anuvartate |
29.d: आत्यन्तिकफलप्रदं मोक्षसंसारमोचनम् । यो ऽनसूयुर् इमं विद्वान् आचारम् अनुवर्तते ।
29.e: 'A learned man who, free from envy, follows this rule of conduct which procures endless rewards, and which through final liberation frees him from transmigration;'

29.s: śraddadhānaḥ śucir dānto dhārayec chruṇuyād api | vihāya sarvapāpāni nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyata iti | nākapṛṣṭhe mahīyata iti |
29.d: श्रद्दधानः शुचिर् दान्तो धारयेच् छ्रुणुयाद् अपि । विहाय सर्वपापानि नाकपृष्ठे महीयत इति । नाकपृष्ठे महीयत इति ।
29.e: 'Or who, full of faith, pure, and subduing his senses, remembers or even hears it, will, freed from all sin, be exalted in the highest heaven.'

30.s: dharmaṃ carata mādharmaṃ satyaṃ vadata mānṛtam | dīrghaṃ paśyata mā hrasvaṃ paraṃ paśyata māparam |
30.d: धर्मं चरत माधर्मं सत्यं वदत मानृतम् । दीर्घं पश्यत मा ह्रस्वं परं पश्यत मापरम् ।
30.e: Practise righteousness, not unrighteousness; speak truth, not untruth; look far, not near; look towards the Highest, not towards that which is not the Highest.
For the Veda (says), 'Agni, forsooth, is a Brāhmaṇa.'

30.s: tatra sado brāhmaṇasya śarīraṃ vediḥ saṃkalpo yajñaḥ paśur ātmā raśanā buddhiḥ sado mukham āhavanīyaṃ nābhyām udaro 'gnir gārhapatyaḥ prāṇo 'dhvaryur apāno hotā vyāno brahmā samāna udgātātmendriyāṇi yajñapātrāṇi ya evaṃ vidvān indriyair indriyārthaṃ juhotīty api ca kāṭhake vijñāyate |
30.d: तत्र सदो ब्राह्मणस्य शरीरं वेदिः संकल्पो यज्ञः पशुर् आत्मा रशना बुद्धिः सदो मुखम् आहवनीयं नाभ्याम् उदरो ऽग्निर् गार्हपत्यः प्राणो ऽध्वर्युर् अपानो होता व्यानो ब्रह्मा समान उद्गातात्मेन्द्रियाणि यज्ञपात्राणि य एवं विद्वान् इन्द्रियैर् इन्द्रियार्थं जुहोतीत्य् अपि च काठके विज्ञायते ।
30.e: And it is also declared in the Kā th aka, 'On that (occasion) the body of the Brāhmaṇa who represents the sacrificial seat is the altar, the vow to perform the rite is the sacrifice, the soul is the animal to be slain, the intellect the rope (with which the animal is bound), the mouth of (the Brāhmaṇa) who represents the seat is the Āhavanīya fire, in his navel (is the Dakshiṇā fire), the fire in his abdomen is the Gārhapatya fire, the Prāṇa is the Adhvaryu priest, the Apāna, the Hot ri priest, the Vyāna the Brahman, the Samāna the Udgāt ri priest, the organs of sensation the sacrificial vessels. He who knowing this offers a sacrifice to the organs through the organs.' . . .

30.s: athāpy udāharanti | pāti trāti ca dātāram ātmānaṃ caiva kilbiṣāt | vedendhanasamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu |
30.d: अथाप्य् उदाहरन्ति । पाति त्राति च दातारम् आत्मानं चैव किल्बिषात् । वेदेन्धनसमृद्धेषु हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु ।
30.e: Now they quote also (the following verses): 'An offering placed in the mouth-fire of a Brāhmaṇa which is rich in Veda-fuel, protects and saves the giver and (the eater) himself from sin.'

30.s: na skandate na vyathate nainam adhyāpatec ca yat | variṣṭham agnihotrāt tu brāhmaṇasya mukhe hutam |
30.d: न स्कन्दते न व्यथते नैनम् अध्यापतेच् च यत् । वरिष्ठम् अग्निहोत्रात् तु ब्राह्मणस्य मुखे हुतम् ।
30.e: 'But the offering made through the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa, which is neither spilt nor causes pain (to sentient creatures), nor assails him (who makes it), is far more excellent than an Agnihotra.'

30.s: dhyānāgniḥ satyopacayanaṃ kṣāntyāhutiḥ sruvaṃ hrīḥ puroḍāśam ahiṃsā saṃtoṣo | yūpaḥ kṛcchraṃ bhūtebhyo 'bhayadākṣiṇyam iti kṛtvā kratu mānasaṃ yāti kṣayaṃ budhaḥ |
30.d: ध्यानाग्निः सत्योपचयनं क्षान्त्याहुतिः स्रुवं ह्रीः पुरोडाशम् अहिंसा संतोषो । यूपः कृच्छ्रं भूतेभ्यो ऽभयदाक्षिण्यम् इति कृत्वा क्रतु मानसं याति क्षयं बुधः ।
30.e: After performing a mental sacrifice at which meditation (takes the place of the sacred) fire, truthfulness (the place of) the sacred fuel, patience (the place of) the oblation, modesty (the place of) the sacrificial spoon, abstention from injuring living beings (the place of the) sacrificial cake, contentment (the place of) the sacrificial post, (and a promise of) safety given to all beings which is hard to keep (the place of) the reward given to the priests, a wise man goes to his (eternal) home.

30.s: jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ | jīvanāśā dhanāśā ca jīryato 'pi na jīryati |
30.d: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः । जीवनाशा धनाशा च जीर्यतो ऽपि न जीर्यति ।
30.e: The hair of an aging man shows signs of age, (and) the teeth of an aging man show signs of age, (but) the desire to live and the desire for wealth do not decay even in an aging man.

30.s: yā dustyajā durmatibhir yā na jīryati jīryataḥ | yāsau prāṇāntiko vyādhis tāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham iti |
30.d: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर् या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः । यासौ प्राणान्तिको व्याधिस् तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् इति ।
30.e: Happiness (is the portion) of that man who relinquishes (all) desire, which fools give up with difficulty, which does not diminish with age, and which is a life-long disease.

30.s: namo 'stu mitrāvaruṇayor urvaśyātmajāya śatayātave vasiṣṭhāya vasiṣṭhāyeti |
30.d: नमो ऽस्तु मित्रावरुणयोर् उर्वश्यात्मजाय शतयातवे वसिष्ठाय वसिष्ठायेति ।
30.e: Adoration to Vasish th a Satayātu, the son of Mitra and Varuṇa and Urvaśī!
